Q: Is there a way to store actual data in Qrcode? A:

Roughly speaking, one black or white dot in a QR code is one bit. A QR code additionally has a certain overhead to it, let's say ~30% on average. A PDF is probably a few hundred kilobyte on average, and can be dozens or hundreds of megabytes large.

So let's take a 300 KB PDF, +30%, is 390 KB. That's 3,120,000 bits, so ~3 million dots that need to be displayed. That would require a QR code with a width and height of ~1733 dots. If each dot is displayed as one pixel on screen, that just about fills an average 1080p computer screen completely (pixel count-wise; from its aspect ratio it would exceed the display height).

In other words: it would be a ginormous QR code, which would be completely unwieldy in practice. If you wanted to print it, you'd have to print it in very fine quality on an A4 sized paper at least, better yet an A1 or A0 paper to give phone camera lenses a chance to actually see all the dots. Which they probably wouldn't anyway.

Q: Match multiple or patterns A:

The issue is that re.findall() expects one regex pattern, not multiple patterns combined with Python OR. In regex, the OR operator is |, not OR.

Also, *JANUARY* is not valid regex syntax the way it is used there.

Correct approach using a regex OR pattern

You can combine the months using | inside the regex:

import re

path = ".../JANUARY/..."

if re.findall(r'(JANUARY|SEPTEMBER|NOVEMBER)', path):
    print(path)
else:
    print('not: JANUARY, SEPTEMBER, NOVEMBER')

Explanation:

  • JANUARY|SEPTEMBER|NOVEMBER → regex OR

  • re.findall() returns matches if any pattern exists.

Better option: use re.search()

If you only want to check whether it exists, re.search() is simpler and faster:

import re

path = ".../JANUARY/..."

if re.search(r'(JANUARY|SEPTEMBER|NOVEMBER)', path):
    print(path)
else:
    print('not: JANUARY, SEPTEMBER, NOVEMBER')

re.search() stops at the first match, so it's usually preferred for condition checks.

If you want to ensure the month is inside the path structure

You can include the slashes:

if re.search(r'/(JANUARY|SEPTEMBER|NOVEMBER)/', path):

I hope this answers your question.

Q: What is the maximum length an Intel 386 instruction without any prefixes? A:

https://www.sandpile.org/x86/opc_enc.htm has the answer.

The traditional limit is indeed 15.

With HLE or XOP, up to 16 became possible.

With APX, up to 17 are possible, both with EVEX and with REX2.
